doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Closing: life as improvisation and recapitulation; thanks
summary: He compares the interview and his life to unscripted play, recalls childhood toy stories, calls himself in recapitulation, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well it’s been a real pleasure for me.

Me too man. You know like this whole interview thing is the same approach I do when I play. You don’t have an idea what you’re going to play. I didn’t have a script. You didn’t have a script. Or you had some ideas with questioning me. But I walked through the door, I didn’t know what was going to happen. I didn’t know what key we were going to be talking in. So that’s the way I like to react to life, you know just okay, let’s see what’s going to happen. And when it’s all over and done I hope you don’t have to do too much editing or whatever. That’s the same with my playing music, to have a flow and the voice and when it’s all over you can see how it’s all connected. As a kid when I used to play on Saturday mornings man I used to love like when I was a kid I had the little plastic cowboys and Indians and the soldiers. And Saturday mornings man, it was beautiful. I’d wake up and I’d fix the covers of my bed to make it look like the mountains, and I always had a great imagination. So I would start my little stories with my toys whatever, and play and from the beginning a story would unfold. I didn’t have a script. And then sometimes the Indians would win, sometimes the cowboys would win, sometimes everybody would get wiped out. But when it was all over it was like a story with a beginning, a middle and an ending, just like the Lone Ranger or whatever or some of that stuff back in those days. So that’s the way I see my life is like that. And that’s the way music is. You have a beginning, a middle and an ending where you state what it is you © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-
develop it and then you recapitulate. So right now my life, I’m in a recapitulation of my life and I hope I have an extended coda.
I do too, a long coda. Lots of repeat signs. Okay.

Yeah man. So I’m just trying to take all my knowledge and bring it to this point right now and make use of all the pain and suffering and happiness too and I can do it. Otherwise it’s been for nothing.
Yeah Monk, thank you. © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
